title: runs/<run-id>/artifacts/data/ra.yaml
description: System risk assessment data (P-14; updated by R-2 and M-3) in the SP 800-30 Rev. 1 terms: purpose, scope, risk model, threat sources and events, vulnerabilities, external and supply chain risk, prioritization and communication. SRA-001 to SRA-003 read it.

statement.title: Purpose of the risk assessment: the information it is to produce

decisions.title: Decisions the risk assessment is intended to support

kind.title: Whether this is an initial or a subsequent risk assessment

update.title: For a subsequent assessment: what prompted the update and the previous report

previous.title: Reference to the previous risk assessment report

point_of_contact.title: Risk assessment point of contact information

persona.title: Persona who is the risk assessment point of contact

name.title: Risk assessment point of contact name

phone.title: Risk assessment point of contact phone number

email.title: Risk assessment point of contact email

applicability.title: Organizational applicability: the tier, systems and parts of the organization the assessment covers

time_frame.title: Effectiveness time frame: how long the results can inform risk-based decisions

architecture.title: Architectural and technology considerations of the scope

assumptions.title: Assumptions under which the risk assessment is conducted

constraints.title: Constraints under which the risk assessment is conducted

information_sources.title: Sources of descriptive, threat, vulnerability and impact information used in the risk assessment

kind.title: What the source informs: descriptive, threat, vulnerability or impact information

title.title: Source of information, such as an Intelligence Community product or the Defense Intelligence Threat Library module

date.title: Date of the source, which shows its timeliness

consultations.title: Intelligence and security credentialed professionals consulted for cyber threat and security inputs

defined_in.title: Where the risk model and analytic approach are defined: the organization's risk management strategy, or this assessment

factors.title: Risk factors of the risk model

scales.title: Value scales of the risk factors

assessment_approach.title: Assessment approach: quantitative, qualitative or semi-quantitative

analysis_approach.title: Risk analysis approach: threat-oriented (threat-based), asset/impact-oriented (asset impact based) or vulnerability-oriented (vulnerability based)

combination.title: Algorithms or rules that combine likelihood values, and likelihood with impact, into a level of risk

time_period.title: Time period that likelihood and impact assessments are associated with: the temporal element of the risk factors

rationale.title: Why this risk model and analytic approach are used

statement.title: Organizational risk tolerance: the level of risk the organization is willing to assume

tiers.title: Risk tolerance levels set at Tier 1, Tier 2 and Tier 3

tolerance.title: Risk tolerance level set at the tier

operational.title: USCYBERCOM and NSA/CSS cyber operational risk tolerances the assessment applies

in_scope.title: Whether the threat source is relevant to the organization and in scope

capability.title: Adversarial threat source capability to initiate a threat event

intent.title: Adversarial threat source intent to initiate a threat event

targeting.title: Adversarial threat source targeting: whether it has targeted or is actively targeting the system

range_of_effects.title: Range of effects from a non-adversarial threat source

description.title: Threat event, with the tactics, techniques and procedures of an adversarial event

threat_sources.title: Threat sources that could initiate the threat event

relevance.title: Relevance of the threat event (Table E-4)

vulnerabilities.title: Vulnerabilities the threat event could exploit

conditions.title: Predisposing conditions affecting the threat event

likelihood_initiation.title: Likelihood of threat event initiation (adversarial) or occurrence (non-adversarial)

likelihood_impact.title: Likelihood that the threat event, once initiated or occurring, results in adverse impact: likelihood of threat event success

likelihood.title: Overall likelihood of the threat event

impacts.title: Adverse impacts: the harm and the affected asset

impact.title: Maximum level of impact of the threat event

risk.title: Level of risk of the threat event: a combination of likelihood and impact

uncertainty.title: Uncertainty associated with the likelihood, impact and risk determinations

threat_scenarios.title: Threat scenarios: how a series of threat events can cause harm

events.title: Threat events of the threat scenario

level_of_detail.title: Level of detail and form in which threats are analyzed: threat events, threat scenarios or both

pervasiveness.title: Pervasiveness of the predisposing condition (Table F-5)

external.title: Risk from connections, external providers and the supply chain

services_provided.title: Whether external security services are provided

connections.title: Connections and information exchange with enabling and other systems outside the authorization boundary, and the risk they introduce

component.title: Boundary component of the connection or external system interface

nss.title: Whether the connected system is a national security system

introduces.title: Vulnerabilities and predisposing conditions the connected or supporting system introduces; empty only when the risk is very low or low and none_rationale says why

risk.title: Level of risk introduced by the connection

end_to_end_impact.title: Impact of a non-NSS component in the end-to-end analysis of risks

none_rationale.title: Why the entry introduces no vulnerability or predisposing condition; required when the list is empty

end_to_end_analysis.title: End-to-end analysis of risks of a space NSS that includes non-NSS components

considered_by.title: Officials who considered the impact of non-NSS components in the end-to-end analysis of risks

coordinated_with.title: Organizations the end-to-end analysis of risks was coordinated with

providers.title: External providers of services and environments to the system

meets_requirements.title: Whether the services are in accordance with the security requirements of the organization

assurance.title: Assurances obtained from the external provider

loss.title: Loss the use of the external provider could create

trust.title: Whether the level of trust in the external provider provides sufficient assurance

response.title: What the organization does when trust in the external provider is insufficient

compensating_controls.title: Compensating controls employed for the external provider

risk_acceptable.title: Whether the risk arising from use of the external services is acceptable

threat_intelligence.title: Threat intelligence used to assess the third party provider or environment

supply_chain.title: Supply chain risk: each supplier of the system's components

priority.title: Order in which the supplier risk is assessed and treated, 1 first, set once the categorization is approved (C-3; dry-run finding F-04-9)

vulnerabilities.title: Supply chain vulnerabilities and predisposing conditions, including those from disposition and from use of external providers; empty only when the risk is very low or low and none_rationale says why

none_rationale.title: Why the entry introduces no vulnerability or predisposing condition; required when the list is empty

nonconforming.title: Systems or components not built to fully meet the policy that are included in the system

component.title: Component not built to fully meet the requirements

selected.title: Solution that offers the best capability versus risk

coordinated_with.title: External organizations the review was coordinated with

method.title: Method for prioritizing risks of similar level, tied to mission and business requirements and risk tolerance

factors.title: What refined the order of risks of similar level

borderline.title: How uncertain or borderline values were assigned to a bin

effect.title: Whether one materializing makes the other more or less likely

communication.title: Communication and sharing of risk assessment results

recipients.title: Organizational stakeholders and decision makers the risk assessment results are communicated to

method.title: Method used to communicate risk assessment results

shared.title: Source information, intermediate results and supporting evidence shared

policy.title: Organizational policy and guidance on communicating and sharing risk-related information

executive_summary.title: Risk assessment executive summary: purpose, synopsis of key findings and recommendations

ai_capabilities.title: AI-enabled capabilities of the system and their use case risk

use_case_risks.title: The use case-specific risks and mitigation requirements

benchmarks.title: Measurable performance benchmarks, aligned to DoW AI policy and NIST or industry AI standards

standard.title: The DoW, NIST or industry AI standard it aligns to

verified_before_deployment.title: How benchmarks and risk remediation are verified satisfactory before deployment

monitoring.title: How the benchmarks are continuously monitored in operation

bias.title: Unintended bias: how it is minimized, detected and monitored, and how stakeholders are notified

minimization.title: How the AI is designed and deployed to minimize unintended bias

detection.title: The techniques that detect and monitor for unintended bias

notification.title: How appropriate stakeholders are notified of detected model bias

components.title: Suitability of third-party and open-source software components, documented with the risk assessment

factors.title: The risk factors addressed when determining suitability

support.title: The stability, activity level and availability of technical support for the component

distribution_integrity.title: The integrity of the distribution source and the provenance of the software

sub_components.title: The security and license obligations of all sub-components

developer_practices.title: Verifiable evidence of the developer's security practices, including vulnerability management and timely remediation

integrity_mechanisms.title: Strong integrity validation mechanisms, such as signed releases and reproducible builds

adversarial_control.title: The potential for adversarial ownership, investment, contribution or control over the project or vendor

trivial.title: Why an open-source component is trivial, so the further review of a non-trivial one does not apply

open_source.title: The further review of a non-trivial open-source component

governance.title: The structure of the project's leadership and commit authority: an established foundation or individuals

community.title: Community activity, the contribution and pull-request review process, the security disclosure policy and the maintainers' track record

license.title: Legal obligations, license compatibility, copyleft and usage that may trigger undesirable conditions, evaluated with security and operational risk

validation.title: Independent third-party testing, evaluation or validation of a commercial product

outcome.title: Whether a validated product is used

program.title: The approved independent assessment program, such as the NIST CMVP or NIAP Common Criteria

reason.title: Why no validated product is used

system_risk.title: The risk designated for the system, consistent with the most severe threat to any individual component or subcomponent, for consideration of requirements, acquisition and T&E (DoDI 8510.01 3.3.a(3), THREAT-001)

set_by.title: The most severe threat to a component: a threat event, an external connection's component or a supply chain risk; required unless the level is designated above every rated threat, where the rationale states why

privacy.title: Privacy risk assessment of a system processing PII (PRIV-007)

processing.title: The nature of the PII processing the privacy risk assessment considers

impact_on_individuals.title: The impact of the processing on individuals

legal_requirements.title: Legal and policy privacy requirements evaluated for applicability

applies.title: Whether the requirement applies to the system

beyond_baseline.title: Obligations the privacy control baseline does not meet, and the separate steps taken for them

baseline_sufficient.title: Why the privacy control baseline meets every obligation of the requirement, when beyond_baseline is empty

requirements.title: ART-REQ requirements that carry the applicable requirement

team.title: Team or individuals conducting the risk assessment, with contact information

rationales.title: Rationale for each risk-related decision taken during the assessment; an empty list is an answer

tailoring.title: Tailoring of the assessment's robustness, explained so the AO knows how far to rely on the results; an empty list states none

aspect.title: What was assessed with less rigor

cause.title: Why: resource constraints or the availability of detailed risk factor information

reliance.title: To what degree the AO can rely on the results it affects

items.description: Trace token: an interview answer (INT-007.A3), an assumption (ASM-012, ASM-BASELINE-001), a product file with optional anchor (product/architecture.md#identity) or an artifact (ART-SSP).
